a CMAC- ADALINE block can be used to improve the performance of the FOC induction motor driver.
the CMAC-ADLINES block can be used to estimate the rotor speed of an induction motor, and the ADALINE block can be used for the rotor resistance estimation.
the proposed method can be used to improve the performance of a sensorless induction motor drive by using an artificial neural network to estimate the rotor speed and rotor resistance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the FOC performance with the on-line and real-time estimation of electrical motor parameters.
the development of a sensorless FOC scheme with an on-line rotor speed and resistance estimator based on an artificial neural network to improve the performance of an induction motor drive.
the design, simulation and experimental implementation of a sensorless field oriented control for an induction motor drive using artificial neural network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CMAC-ADLNE neural network is a very good alternative in order to improve the performance of an induction motor drive, especially when a high performance is required.

the proposed CMAC-ADLINE based estimator has a better performance in the estimation of the electrical parameters of an induction motor, which in turn improves the overall performance of a field oriented controlled three-phase induction motor driver.

the use of a CMAC-ALADINE block in the standard F.O.C. scheme improves the IM driver performance, especially in terms of the torque response and the torque ripple, which are two of the most important factors to consider in the design of a high-performance drive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CMAC-ADLNE block has been used in a standard FOC algorithm to estimate the rotor speed and rotor resistance of an IM.

the proposed scheme can be used for the real-time and online estimation of the induction motor speed and rotor resistance in a FOC scheme, and it can be used in a real-time and on line estimation of the induction machine parameters, which is the most challenging task in a FOC system.
the proposed method can improve the sensorless FOC performance and can be used in high performance industrial applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CMAC-ADLINE block is able to provide a better speed and rotor resistance estimation than the traditional PI controller.
the rotor resistance and rotor speed are the most sensitive parameters in the FOC scheme.

the proposed neural network-based estimator is able to improve the IM performance, since the speed and rotor resistance are estimated in real time, and the motor is not affected by any parameter changes.
